Your Meta Ads dashboard and your order list probably don't agree.

That isn't a glitch. If you rely only on the Meta Pixel, you're relying on the browser, and ad blockers, privacy settings and simple loading errors all get in the way.

The Meta Conversions API sends your conversions from your server instead. Meta recommends running it alongside the Pixel, sending the same events through both.

In my new guide I cover:

What CAPI actually is, in plain English.
Pixel vs CAPI, and why it isn't either or.
Four setup routes: platform integrations, the Conversions API Gateway, server side Google Tag Manager and a direct API connection.
How event_id and event_name stop Meta counting the same sale twice.
Why hashed customer details lift your Event Match Quality.
How to test everything in Events Manager before you trust a number.

If you spend seriously on Meta Ads, your algorithm is only as smart as the data you feed it. Missing conversions means it learns from half the story.
